blocker_definition: A finding is a FINAL CERTIFICATION BLOCKER only if it prevents the system from reliably answering: What changed? / What is affected? / What evidence remains valid? / What must run? / What actually ran? / What happened? / What was not tested? / What remains uncertain? / Is the result certifiable?

findings.title: Live CI evidence emission not wired into workflows
findings.reasoning: Emission schema, binding derivation, canonical conversion, semantic equivalence are fully implemented and tested (36 C42.29 tests pass). Only the wiring into live GitHub Actions workflows is absent, and that requires a GitHub Actions environment. Does not prevent answering any of the nine questions for locally-derivable evidence.

findings.title: Shared-infrastructure change requires explicit shared:: prefix (no auto-detection)
findings.reasoning: When shared:: prefix is used, R-SRC-002 invalidates exactly the named dependents and the planner re-measures only them. Without the prefix, a shared-module file change does not auto-propagate. This is a deliberately deferred optimization (constraint: do not redesign dependency inference in M38.6). Explicitly-declared changes are answered reliably; auto-detection is an enhancement, not a blocker.

findings.title: Class-E escalation threshold not empirically calibrated
findings.reasoning: The Class-E ESCALATION contract is defined and enforced (Class-E always refused pending human review). Empirical threshold conditions (observation_count>=3, independent_change_count>=2) require real historical accumulation. The system still answers 'what remains uncertain' (escalation pending) without calibration.

findings.title: Forensic-aware cache layer not implemented
findings.reasoning: The base VerificationCache cannot turn a stored failure into a pass (G15 PASS). A component-scoped forensic-aware wrapper is recommended but not required; certification is already safe.

findings.title: SurvivorRegistry for persistent cross-run survivor tracking not implemented
findings.reasoning: Per-run survivor classification and proposal generation work without a persistent registry. A registry improves longitudinal intelligence but is not required to answer the nine questions for the current state.

findings.title: Class-A acceptance lacks completed empirical approval/rejection cycle
findings.reasoning: Class-A proposals are generated and the human-authorization boundary is enforced. No full real approval cycle has completed, but this is a data-accumulation matter, not a structural blocker. Recorded as INSUFFICIENT_DATA, not as a verification failure.

findings.title: 60.297% is mathematically reconciled, not a fresh measurement
findings.reasoning: Explicitly labelled MATHEMATICALLY_RECONCILED throughout C42.26-38. The distinction is enforced in code (labelled aggregates) and in artifacts. Accepted as the correct representation of the evidence state.

findings.title: Historical calibration partial (B/D supported; A/E provisional)
findings.reasoning: Behavioral refusal classes (B, C, D) are empirically supported; acceptance/escalation thresholds await data. This is an observability/calibration improvement, not a blocker.
